steps.body: Flat shapes lie on paper. Solid shapes such as a ball, box, or cone take up space and can be held.
steps.narration: Flat shapes lie on paper. Solid shapes such as a ball, box, or cone take up space and can be held.

widget.prompt: Sort each shape: flat or solid?

items.label: triangle
items.feedback: A triangle lies flat on the page — it is a 2D shape.

items.label: cube
items.feedback: A cube takes up space and has flat faces — it is 3D.

items.label: circle
items.feedback: A circle is flat, with no thickness at all.

items.label: sphere
items.feedback: A sphere is solid and round all over — it is 3D.

widget.missFeedback: Ask whether it could be picked up, or only drawn.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted — flat shapes lie on the page, solids take up space.

predict.prompt: Can a solid shape lie completely flat on the page?

options.label: Yes — a ball and a circle are the same shape

predict.reveal: A solid has thickness, so it cannot lie flat the way a drawn shape does — a picture of a ball is flat, but the ball itself is not.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s compose solid.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

explanationVariants: Flat shapes lie on the page.

widget.prompt: Is a sphere a flat (2D) shape or a solid (3D) shape?

options.label: 3D
options.feedback: Correct — a sphere is a solid: it takes up space and cannot lie flat on the page.

options.label: 2D
options.feedback: A sphere has thickness, so it is a solid rather than a flat shape.

options.label: Neither
options.feedback: Every shape here is either flat or solid; a sphere is one of them.

options.label: Both at once
options.feedback: A shape is flat or solid, not both; a sphere takes up space.

steps.narration: Solids can have flat faces, curved surfaces, or both. The picture compares a cube, cone, and cylinder.

widget.prompt: Tap the shape that takes up space (a solid).

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: A square is flat — it lies on the page with no thickness.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: A triangle is a flat shape, not a solid.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A circle is flat; the solid version of it would be a sphere.

widget.missFeedback: Ask which one could be picked up rather than only drawn.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a cube takes up space, so it is a solid (3D) shape.

steps.body: Match a solid to an object.
explanationVariants: A ball is a familiar sphere-shaped solid.
A sphere is round in every direction, like a ball.

widget.prompt: Which object is shaped like a sphere?

options.label: A ball
options.feedback: Correct — a ball is shaped like a sphere and can roll in every direction.

options.label: A sheet of paper
options.feedback: A sheet is flat, while a sphere is a solid that takes up space.

options.label: A box
options.feedback: A box is shaped like a cube or rectangular prism, not a sphere.

options.label: An ice-cream cone
options.feedback: An ice-cream cone is cone-shaped, with a point and one flat circular face.

hints: A sphere is round all over.
Think of an object that rolls in every direction.

explanationVariants: A cone has 1 flat circular face at its base.
Its other surface is curved, so only the base counts as flat.

widget.prompt: How many flat faces does a cone have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the curved surface too. A cone has 1 flat circular face.
Look at the circular base: it is the cone's 1 flat face.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Find the flat circular base. The curved surface is not a flat face.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — a cone has 1 flat circular face.

hints: Count only flat faces, not curved surfaces.
